historical_thesis.title: A Public-Coin Credential-Based Range Proof with Reusable Commitments
historical_thesis.basis: Algorithm numbers and historical reference tables; current benchmarks use randomized inputs.

intentional_differences: domain-separated SHA-256 counter sampler drives deterministic Durstenfeld shuffling instead of ChaCha12
canonical Java proof encoding follows paper element-count accounting and is not Rust-byte-compatible
outer Section 5.2 T-time Merkle wrapper omitted
paper Algorithm 1 exact-power boundary uses b^i <= x, correcting the recorded Rust snapshot strict-loop edge case
branch selection verifies digit-wise dominance instead of relying only on numeric ordering
zero is represented by one significant zero digit for the artifact input domain [0,2^bits)

paper.title: HashWires: Hyperefficient Credential-Based Range Proofs
basis: Section 3: Commit, Prove, and Verify structure
Section 4.1.2: deterministic padded sparse Merkle tree
Section 4.2: shared multichains and per-MDP salts
Appendix B: deterministic KDFs and Durstenfeld shuffling

note: Source lineage and recorded upstream snapshot identifiers. The upstream archives are provenance references and are not required to build or run this source distribution. The HashWires Java port is a derivative implementation, not a byte-identical retained Rust snapshot.
